title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 3 and 4.
This question paper consists of 9 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: Common Fractions and Decimal Fractions

questions.prompt: Simplify $\dfrac{18}{24}$.
questions.explanation: Divide by the HCF $6$: $\frac{3}{4}$. The other options $\frac{9}{12}$ and $\frac{6}{8}$ are equivalent but not fully simplified.

questions.prompt: Calculate $2\dfrac{1}{2} \times 1\dfrac{1}{3}$.

questions.explanation: $0{,}3 = 0{,}30$, and $30$ hundredths is more than $25$ hundredths.

questions.prompt: Calculate $0{,}6 \times 0{,}4$.
questions.explanation: $6 \times 4 = 24$; two decimal places in total, so $0{,}24$.

questions.prompt: Calculate $7{,}2 \div 0{,}09$.
questions.explanation: Multiply both by 100: $720 \div 9 = 80$.

questions.prompt:
Lindiwe spends $\frac{1}{3}$ of her money on food and $\frac{1}{4}$ on transport.
(a) What fraction of her money is left?  (2)
(b) If she had R720, how much is left?  (2)
For $y = 2x - 1$, find $y$ when $x = 4$.

(a) Complete a table of values for $y = -2x + 3$ for $x = -1;\ 0;\ 1;\ 2;\ 3$.  (2)
(b) Write down the coordinates of the $y$-intercept and the $x$-intercept.  (2)
In a right-angled triangle, which side is the hypotenuse?
options: The side next to the right angle
The side opposite the right angle
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle; it is always the longest side.

questions.prompt: A triangle with sides 7, 24 and 25 is right-angled.
A triangle with sides 4, 5 and 6 is right-angled.
questions.explanation: $4^2 + 5^2 = 41$, but $6^2 = 36$. They are not equal.

questions.prompt: A 5 m ladder leans against a vertical wall with its foot 1,4 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach, in metres?
Which set of numbers is a Pythagorean triple?
A rectangle is 9 cm wide and 12 cm long. Calculate the length of its diagonal, in cm.
A square has sides of 10 cm. Calculate the length of its diagonal, correct to two decimal places.
$\triangle KLM$ has $KL = 9$ cm, $LM = 40$ cm and $KM = 41$ cm. Is the triangle right-angled? If so, at which vertex is the right angle?
questions.memo:
$9^2 + 40^2 = 81 + 1\ 600 = 1\ 681$ ✓ (1)
$41^2 = 1\ 681$, so yes, it is right-angled ✓ (1)
The right angle is opposite $KM$, at $L$ ✓ (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 4: Perimeter and Area of 2D Shapes

questions.prompt: Calculate the area of a circle with radius 5 cm. Use the $\pi$ key and round to two decimal places.

questions.explanation: $1\ \text{m}^2 = 100\ \text{cm} \times 100\ \text{cm} = 10\ 000\ \text{cm}^2$.

questions.prompt: Match each shape with its area formula.
questions.explanation: These four formulae must be known by heart.

questions.prompt: The side of a square is doubled. What happens to its area?
questions.explanation: $(2s)^2 = 4s^2$: the area is multiplied by $2^2 = 4$.

questions.prompt: A circle has a circumference of 31,4 cm. Using $\pi = 3{,}14$, calculate its diameter.
A triangle has an area of $24\ \text{cm}^2$ and a base of 8 cm. Calculate its perpendicular height.

sections.title: QUESTION 5: Surface Area and Volume of 3D Objects

questions.prompt: Match each volume with the equal capacity.
questions.explanation: $1\ \text{cm}^3 = 1$ ml, so $1\ 000\ \text{cm}^3 = 1$ litre and $1\ \text{m}^3 = 1\ 000\ 000\ \text{cm}^3 = 1\ 000$ litres.

questions.prompt: How many cubes with 2 cm edges fit exactly into a box measuring 10 cm by 6 cm by 4 cm?
questions.explanation: $5$ along the length, $3$ across and $2$ up: $5 \times 3 \times 2 = 30$. (Or $240 \div 8 = 30$.)

questions.prompt: A triangular prism has right-angled triangles with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm at its ends, and is 10 cm long. Calculate its total surface area.
Describe the transformation $(x;\ y) \to (x + 3;\ y - 1)$.
options: Translation 3 units right and 1 unit down
Translation 3 units left and 1 unit up
questions.explanation: Adding 3 to $x$ moves right; subtracting 1 from $y$ moves down.

questions.prompt: Match each rule with the transformation it describes.
questions.explanation: Learn these rules and check each one by sketching a point.

questions.prompt: How many edges does a triangular prism have?
questions.explanation: 3 edges on each triangle (6) plus 3 edges joining them: 9.

questions.prompt: A cylinder is a polyhedron.
questions.explanation: A cylinder has a curved surface. Polyhedra have only flat polygon faces.

questions.prompt: Which Platonic solid has 8 equilateral triangles as faces?
questions.explanation: *Octa* means 8: the octahedron.

questions.prompt: How many vertices does a cube have?
questions.explanation: 4 corners on the top and 4 on the bottom: 8.

questions.prompt: All the faces of a Platonic solid are the same regular polygon.
questions.explanation: That is part of the definition of a Platonic solid.

questions.prompt: Which object has two flat circular faces and one curved surface?
questions.explanation: A cylinder (like a tin) has a circle at each end and a curved side.

questions.prompt: What is the name for a 3D object whose faces are all flat polygons?
questions.explanation: A polyhedron has only flat polygon faces.

questions.prompt: Describe the net of a triangular prism: which shapes does it contain, and how many of each?
questions.memo:
2 triangles ✓ (1)
3 rectangles (joined in a row, with a triangle on two opposite sides) ✓ (1)

questions.prompt: Find the mean of $4;\ 7;\ 8;\ 10;\ 11$.
Find the median of $3;\ 9;\ 5;\ 12;\ 7$.
questions.explanation: Ordered: $3;\ 5;\ 7;\ 9;\ 12$. The middle value is $7$.

questions.prompt: Which type of graph is best for showing how a whole is divided into parts?
questions.explanation: A pie chart shows each category as a fraction of the whole circle.

questions.prompt: In a histogram, the bars touch each other.
questions.explanation: A histogram shows continuous class intervals, so there are no gaps between the bars.

questions.prompt: One very large value is added to a data set. Which measure changes the most?
questions.explanation: The mean uses the size of every value, so an outlier pulls it strongly. The median only moves a little.

questions.prompt: To find out what the whole school thinks about the uniform, it is fair to ask only the Grade 12 learners.
questions.explanation: That sample is biased: it leaves out Grades 8 to 11, who may think differently.

questions.prompt: The mean of five numbers is $12$. Four of the numbers are $10$, $14$, $9$ and $15$. Find the fifth number.
A probability can be equal to $1{,}2$.
questions.explanation: Probabilities are always between $0$ and $1$ (inclusive).

questions.prompt: A coin is tossed and a die is rolled. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
questions.explanation: $2 \times 6 = 12$ outcomes (H1 to H6 and T1 to T6).

questions.prompt: What happens to the relative frequency of an event as an experiment is repeated many more times?
options: It gets further from the theoretical probability
It gets closer to the theoretical probability
questions.explanation: Over many trials, the relative frequency settles close to the theoretical probability.

questions.prompt:
Two dice are rolled and the numbers are added.
(a) How many outcomes are in the sample space?  (1)
(b) In how many ways can the total be 7?  (1)
(c) Find $P(\text{total} = 7)$ and $P(\text{total} = 12)$.  (2)
The letters of the word MATHEMATICS are written on 11 cards and one card is chosen at random. Find $P(\text{M})$ and $P(\text{vowel})$.
